main_body: Altar drawn as a white block with a lilac cloth panel and gold cross above, then a purple front face with a gold cross and gold hem, on a light grey base
top_band: White area at rows 11-23, with a lilac panel and cross drawn face-on. It reads as a vertical face (a backpiece or panel), not a horizontal top. Only a gold band at rows 24-25 and a brown line at row 25 mark an edge.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the white region at rows 11-23 carries a cross on a cloth panel, so it is a vertical face. It is not a top surface seen from above. The true horizontal edge is just the 2-row gold/brown band at rows 24-25, which is a rim. The purple front face below (rows 26-35) is painted flat with a cross and vertical fold stripes, not inset. The object is a flat front elevation with no real top band, so it fails.

style.evidence: The large white area (about 18x12 px) is a single flat fill. The grey base is nearly flat too. The purple cloth has only about 3-4 tones, with simple stripes and no grain or speckle. There is no tinted outline, and forms are separated only by value. Next to the cheese stall and the roofed well, which have rich per-tile detail, the altar is much thinner and flatter. Most tiles hold only 2-4 colours.
